description: AixWeather provides a Python workflow for preparing weather inputs for building-energy simulations. RWTH Aachen University develops it to retrieve source weather, transform units and time conventions, fill selected variables and export simulation formats. The README lists DWD historical observations for German stations and MOSMIX forecasts for worldwide stations, alongside reference-year, EPW and local-station inputs. Coverage and available dates depend on the selected source; the stated temporal limitation is hourly data. The code is available on GitHub and PyPI, and a web application is documented. Outputs include EnergyPlus EPW, Modelica ReaderTMY3 and unconverted CSV or JSON core data. The repository LICENSE and README state BSD-3-Clause, allowing free software reuse. Some upstream data sources require separate access, and the README warns about variable quality in reference-year datasets. Those caveats should be checked before calibrating or testing a building model. Related record model-energyplus can consume the documented EPW output. This review verified metadata and the workflow description, without retrieving weather datasets or running conversions.
